newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWIMMING-POLL OUTSTANDING AT WORLD MEET.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-POLL OUTSTANDING AT WORLD MEET.

text.p: Two superlative world records by Claudia Poll provided the highlights of the world short-course swimming championships which saw Australia top the medals table and the Chinese women's team back in business.

Costa Rican Olympic champion Poll reached new heights in retaining her 200 and 400 metres freestyle crowns in the 25-metre pool in the Scandinavium indoor arena which was erected in less than three days for the championships and then dismantled.

In the space of 24 hours Poll sliced 1.25 seconds from her own 200 world mark and 2.02 seconds from the 10-year-old world record of East German Astrid Strauss in the 400, setting impressive new standards of 1:54.17 and 4:00.03 for the two distances.
Australia led the way in the medals table with nine golds, two silvers and eight bronzes, a performance full of a promise for a youthful team.
Kristy Ellem inherited the two women's breaststroke titles of her training partner Samantha Riley and fellow 15-year-old Natasha Bowron romped away in the 800 metres freestyle.

Grant Hackett and Emma Johnson, both 16, established themselves as gold medallists in the men's 1,500 freestyle and women's 400 individual medley, while 23-year-old Matthew Dunn ensured he was not upstaged by the youngsters by repeating his 1995 title double in the 200 and 400 individual medley.

China, who retreated from their previous commanding heights at last year's Olympics in the wake of doping scandals in 1994, bounced back with six golds, five silvers and two bronzes -- all but two silvers courtesy of the women's team.

China dominated the women's events at the 1994 world long- course championships in Rome, winning 12 of the 16 women's titles, but the gold lost some of its glitter a month later when seven Chinese swimmers returned positive dope tests at the Asian Games in Japan.

China achieved a more modest medal haul at the 1996 Atlanta Olympics with one gold, three silvers and two bronzes but they look set to make a bigger splash at the next major global meeting -- the world long-course championships in Perth, Australia, next January.

They cracked two of their own women's relay world records and missed a third by just 0.10 seconds, giving ample evidence of their strength and potential even in the absence of many top competitors at these championships.

Olympic champion Le Jingyi lost both her individual titles, finishing third in the 50 and 100 freestyle she won at the two previous editions of the championships, but turned in the fastest 100 freestyle of the meeting as lead-off swimmer in a relay.
Liu Limin, double world long-course champion in 1994, won the women's 200 butterfly and Lu Donghua and Chen Yan emerged as new champions in the women's 100 and 200 backstroke.
Eight world short-course records fell -- two to Poll, two to China in women's relays, two to Australia in men's relays and two to Americans Misty Hyman and Jenny Thompson in a single race.
Hyman displayed a largely submarine style in butterfly, swimming much of the race kicking sideways under water, and broke the 50 butterfly mark.

Unfortunately for Hyman, Thompson and China's Cai Huijue passed her in the second half of the race and Thompson claimed the 100 title with all three swimming inside the old world record for the full distance.
